name: Ruchi Sanghvi
category: Software engineer, Facebook early engineer, investor
milestone_by_age_26: In 2005 at age 23 she joined Facebook as its first female engineer; in September 2006 at age 24 she was a primary engineer on the first News Feed launch and authored the launch blog post.
early_history_summary: Raised in Pune, India, intending to join her father's business after studies. Earned BS and MS in electrical and computer engineering at Carnegie Mellon (graduated 2004), briefly worked at Oracle in Silicon Valley, then joined early Facebook in 2005 with partner Aditya Agarwal. She shipped News Feed, later Platform/Connect work, left in 2010 to cofound Cove (acquired by Dropbox 2012), and later founded South Park Commons.
primary_leverage_engine: Technical depth + product execution at early Facebook
family_context_summary: Raised in Pune; as a youth she expected to join her father's business after school. Detailed parental occupations and wealth not richly documented beyond that business-family path.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father ran a business she was expected to join; not documented as a software/engineering apprenticeship path.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CMU engineering, early Facebook hire, Silicon Valley move, News Feed shipping, partner Agarwal
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, BBC, and CMU profiles agree she joined Facebook in 2005 as first female engineer at ~23 and was a primary engineer on News Feed (Sept 2006) at ~24. CMU pipeline and Bay Area move with Agarwal concentrated opportunity; family business background is noted but not a software-domain apprenticeship. Later Cove/Dropbox/South Park Commons extend operator trajectory.
starting_point: Born 20 January 1982 in Pune, India; raised with expectation of joining father's business; trained in electrical/computer engineering at Carnegie Mellon.
current_position: Co-head and general partner of South Park Commons (tech community and fund); former Facebook first female engineer, Cove cofounder, Dropbox VP of Operations; has served on boards including Paytm and UCSF.

trajectory.event: Completed Carnegie Mellon BS/MS path and entered Silicon Valley (Oracle), then pivoted toward early social-tech roles.
Joined Facebook as its first female engineer alongside Aditya Agarwal.
Primary engineer on the first News Feed; wrote the public launch post amid user backlash and privacy fixes.
Left Facebook and cofounded collaboration startup Cove with Agarwal.
Cove acquired by Dropbox; she joined Dropbox and later became VP of Operations.
Founded South Park Commons, a SF technical community later with an associated fund.

family_context_summary: Parents named Winfried and Kristin (Grüner) Thrun; detailed class/wealth not documented in reviewed sources.

milestone_by_age_26: BS Michigan 1993 (~21–22) and Berkeley PhD 1999 (~27–28); major awards (Mark Weiser 2018, ACM Fellow 2020) and OSTEP textbook impact come well after 26—no material research milestone dated by age 26 found.

family_context_summary: Born in Ann Arbor; father Vedat S. Arpaci was a longtime mechanical engineering professor—academic family environment noted in secondary profiles.

evidence_summary: Goodreads/public records and UW/Michigan profiles support ~1971 birth and 1993/1999 degrees; PhD and faculty impact after age 26. Ordinary undergrad completion is not treated as the qualifying material milestone.

name: Leslie Lamport
milestone_by_age_26: MIT BS mathematics 1960 (age 19) and Brandeis MA 1963 (age 22) are strong academic steps, but seminal CS results (e.g., Time/Clocks 1978, Byzantine Generals 1982, LaTeX 1980s, Turing Award 2013) and industry research posts (Mass Computer Associates from 1970, age ~29) arrived after 26; no dated material CS research/product milestone by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born Brooklyn Jewish immigrant family; Bronx High School of Science; MIT math BS 1960; Brandeis MA 1963 and PhD 1972 (analytic PDEs). Shifted into industrial computing research that founded distributed-systems theory.
family_context_summary: Son of Benjamin and Hannah Lamport (née Lasser); father immigrant from Russian Empire, mother from Austro-Hungarian Empire/Poland region.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a computing-domain family apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and ACM Turing materials place breakthrough distributed-systems work and LaTeX well after age 26. Early MIT degree alone is not coded as the qualifying material career milestone under strict rules.

early_history_summary: BS Physics and Information/Computer Science at UC Irvine; MS/PhD physics Carnegie Mellon; UCSB postdoc; KU faculty 1993 focusing on b/c quarks, silicon detectors (D0, CMS), Higgs discovery collaboration, neutrino radio detectors, and Quarked! outreach.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and KU profiles show a standard physics research career with major collaboration milestones (e.g., Higgs 2012 era, APS Fellow 2011) long after any plausible age-26 window for a 1993 faculty start.

name: Adam Paszke
milestone_by_age_26: In 2016 at about age 20–21, while a University of Warsaw CS/Math student on a FAIR internship under Soumith Chintala, he co-created and shipped the initial PyTorch release (alpha September 2016) as an original author of the framework.
early_history_summary: Polish student of computer science and mathematics at University of Warsaw (MIMUW). Reached out for FAIR internships in early 2016, joined the small LuaTorch team, and with Sam Gross, Soumith Chintala, and Gregory Chanan built the Python-first Torch redesign that became PyTorch. Later research scientist roles at Google/DeepMind; work on compilers and languages (e.g., Pallas, Mosaic, dex-lang).
primary_early_advantage_tags: FAIR internship, Soumith mentorship, open-source Torch community, University of Warsaw, deep learning wave
evidence_summary: PyTorch Wikipedia lists Paszke among original authors with September 2016 release; Soumith Chintala's design-origins post and secondary histories state the project began as Paszke's FAIR internship. Batch birth year 1995 implies age ~21 at first release—well under 26. Family background undocumented; primary advantages are elite lab embedding, complementary FAIR collaborators, and the deep-learning tooling wave.
starting_point: Not fully documented; studied CS and mathematics at University of Warsaw (Poland) before and during the FAIR internship that produced PyTorch.
current_position: Principal/research scientist path at Google DeepMind; original PyTorch author still associated with ML systems and compiler research (Pallas/Mosaic/related work).

trajectory.event: As a FAIR intern and University of Warsaw student, co-authored the first PyTorch releases that ported Torch ideas to Python with autograd-first design.
Continued core maintenance as PyTorch adoption accelerated across research labs and industry.
Lead author on the NeurIPS paper formalizing PyTorch's design; framework became a default research stack.
OpenAI standardized on PyTorch for major models, cementing ecosystem dominance.
PyTorch moved under the Linux Foundation's PyTorch Foundation after Meta spin-out governance shift.
PyTorch 2.0 released with compiler stack (TorchDynamo); Paszke continued advanced systems research at Google.

name: Rajive Bagrodia
milestone_by_age_26: IIT Bombay BTech then UT Austin MA (1983) and PhD (1987); UCLA professor from ~1987; founded Scalable Network Technologies in 1999; NSF Presidential Young Investigator 1991—no birth year and no clear material milestone dated by age 26.
early_history_summary: Indian-American CS researcher focused on wireless networks, parallel/distributed simulation (Maisie, Parsec, GloMoSim). Academic career at UCLA then commercialized network simulation via Scalable Network Technologies; emeritus professor.
evidence_summary: UCLA/Samueli bio gives MA 1983 and PhD 1987 and company founding 1999; without birth year, PhD and PYI awards still align with a standard post-doc academic arc rather than a verified ≤26 material breakout.
